selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes
experiences.description: Hit the world-renowned slopes of the Jungfrau region, offering over 200km of groomed runs suitable for all skill levels. Families can enjoy beginner-friendly runs in Grindelwald while advanced skiers tackle the challenging Lauberhorn descent. Ski school lessons for kids are available and highly recommended for younger family members.

experiences.name: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride
experiences.description: Board the iconic Glacier Express, one of the world's most scenic train journeys, traveling through dramatic Alpine landscapes, frozen valleys, and snow-covered peaks. The 8-hour panoramic ride connects Zermatt to St. Moritz and is a magical, relaxing experience perfect for families wanting to soak in Swiss Alpine beauty without physical exertion.
experiences.location: Zermatt to St. Moritz, Valais & Graubünden

experiences.name: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Experience
experiences.description: Join a local Alpine cheesemaker for a hands-on fondue and raclette cooking class in a traditional mountain chalet. Learn the centuries-old art of Swiss cheese production, taste regional varieties, and enjoy a hearty communal fondue dinner with locally sourced bread and charcuterie. A culturally immersive and delicious family activity.

experiences.name: Family Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking Adventure
experiences.description: Explore pristine snow-covered Alpine forests and meadows on a guided family snowshoeing tour. Trails around Saas-Fee are well-marked and suitable for children aged 5 and up. Guides share fascinating facts about Alpine wildlife and ecosystems. The tour concludes with hot chocolate and traditional Swiss pastries at a cozy mountain hut.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch Natural Toboggan Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly winter activities on a natural toboggan run. The 3km illuminated night run near Davos is an unforgettable adrenaline rush for kids and adults alike. Sleds are available for rent on-site, and the run is safe, well-maintained, and accessible for children as young as 6 years old.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Swiss Alps, Switzerland

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 22:30 via Flight UA. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) train from Zurich Airport to your destination in the Swiss Alps (approximately 1.5-2.5 hours depending on exact location). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Unpack and get settled. Rest up for the exciting week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the Zurich Airport food court or a convenience snack from a Migros/Coop airport kiosk (budget CHF 10-15). Alternatively, pack snacks for the train ride.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass or regional day passes at the airport for cost-effective travel throughout the week. The SBB train is the most budget-friendly option from Zurich Airport. Keep receipts for all transport for potential VAT refunds. Set alarms early for Day 2 — the adventure begins!

day_by_day.morning: After a good night's rest, enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Head out to explore the local ski area. Purchase a budget day ski pass (look for beginner or half-day passes to save money — typically CHF 30-50 vs CHF 60-80 for full day). Rent ski equipment from a local rental shop rather than resort-owned shops to save 20-30%. Beginners can take a 2-hour group ski lesson (CHF 40-60 per person), which is far cheaper than private lessons.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on beginner to intermediate slopes. Explore the ski area map and identify free or low-cost runs accessible with your pass. Take a scenic gondola or chairlift ride even if not skiing to soak in the breathtaking Alpine panoramas. Visit the ski village on foot to get oriented with local shops, restaurants, and amenities.
day_by_day.evening: Return ski equipment if renting daily. Warm up with a traditional Swiss fondue at a local mountain hut or village restaurant. Look for set menus or 'Tagesmenü' (daily specials) which offer the best value — typically CHF 18-25 for a full meal. Stroll through the illuminated village center and plan the rest of the week's activities.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort (included if possible) or pick up fresh bread and yogurt from a local Coop or Migros supermarket (CHF 5-8)
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich and thermos of hot chocolate from the supermarket to eat on the slopes — saves CHF 15-20 vs mountain restaurant prices
meals.dinner: Local village restaurant — order the 'Tagesmenü' (daily special) for CHF 18-25. Try Rösti (Swiss potato dish) or a hearty Alpine soup for budget-friendly authentic Swiss cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Always compare ski rental prices between at least 2-3 shops. Intersport and Sport Check chains often offer competitive rates. Book group ski lessons in advance online for early-bird discounts. Layer up with thermal base layers — Alpine temperatures in February can drop to -10°C to -15°C.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, head to the famous Fläsch Natural Toboggan Run — one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly winter experiences. The natural toboggan run uses the actual mountain terrain, making it a unique and authentic Swiss winter activity. Toboggan rentals are very affordable (CHF 5-15 per sled) and the run itself is either free or low-cost (CHF 5-10). Spend the morning making multiple runs down the slope — it's great fun for all ages and completely budget-friendly compared to ski passes.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the toboggan run, explore the charming village of Fläsch or the surrounding area. Visit a local bakery for a warm treat. If energy permits, try snowshoeing — a very affordable winter activity (CHF 10-20 for snowshoe rental) that allows you to explore pristine Alpine forests and meadows at your own pace. No lessons required, making it ideal for families and beginners.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Cook a simple meal in the resort kitchen if facilities are available using supermarket groceries — this is the biggest budget saver of the trip. Alternatively, visit a local Migros Restaurant (Switzerland's budget-friendly supermarket chain restaurant) for a hot meal at CHF 12-18 per person. Enjoy a family board game night or hot cocoa by the fireplace.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket groceries — muesli, milk, fresh fruit, and Swiss bread (CHF 4-6 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at the toboggan run — hot soup in a thermos, sandwiches, energy bars, and hot drinks. Budget CHF 5-8 per person
meals.dinner: Migros Restaurant or cook at resort using supermarket groceries. Budget CHF 10-15 per person for a hearty pasta or rice dish with Swiss cheese

day_by_day.notes: The Fläsch Natural Toboggan Run is best experienced in the morning when snow conditions are freshest. Wear waterproof trousers and gloves — tobogganing is a wet activity! Children must be supervised at all times. Check local tourism office for any free or discounted family activity passes available mid-week.

day_by_day.morning: Purchase a multi-day ski pass if you haven't already — 3-day or 5-day passes offer significant savings over daily passes (often 15-25% cheaper per day). Head back to the slopes with renewed energy. Focus on improving skiing technique on intermediate runs. Many Swiss resorts offer free ski patrol-led orientation tours on Wednesday and Thursday mornings — check at the ski school office.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try a different winter sport in the afternoon — ice skating at the local outdoor rink is typically CHF 5-10 for entry plus CHF 5-8 for skate rental, making it one of the most affordable Alpine activities. Alternatively, try cross-country skiing (Langlauf) on the free or low-cost groomed trails that many Swiss villages maintain — equipment rental is CHF 15-25, much cheaper than downhill skiing.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local tourism office or resort concierge to pick up free maps and brochures about free attractions and events happening in the area. Attend any free village events, live music, or cultural performances that may be scheduled. Many Swiss Alpine villages host free weekly events during ski season. Enjoy dinner at a local Beizli (traditional Swiss pub/restaurant) and try Raclette — a shared meal that's both authentic and reasonably priced.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or supermarket staples
meals.lunch: Mountain self-service restaurant — choose the soup and bread option (CHF 8-12) rather than full meals. Share dishes between family members to reduce costs
meals.dinner: Local Beizli — Raclette or Käseschnitzel (cheese schnitzel) with a local beer or soft drink. Budget CHF 20-28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Multi-day ski passes purchased at tourist offices in the village center are sometimes cheaper than buying directly at the ski lift. Ask about family packages — children under 9 often ski free with a paying adult in many Swiss resorts. Keep your ski pass safe as replacements can be costly.

day_by_day.morning: Take advantage of free winter hiking trails — many Swiss Alpine communities maintain well-marked winter walking paths that are completely free and offer stunning mountain scenery. Rent snowshoes (CHF 10-20) and explore the backcountry terrain around the resort. Visit a local farm or dairy to see how traditional Swiss cheese and chocolate are made — many offer free or very low-cost tours and tastings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local Swiss Alpine Museum or cultural center if available — many offer free or reduced admission on weekdays. Alternatively, explore a nearby traditional Swiss village on foot, visiting the local church, town square, and historic buildings at no cost. Browse local artisan shops for affordable Swiss souvenirs like Swiss chocolate (CHF 2-5 per bar) rather than expensive watches or branded items.
day_by_day.evening: Host a 'Swiss night' in the resort room — purchase Swiss fondue ingredients from the supermarket (cheese, bread, wine or grape juice) for CHF 15-20 total and make your own fondue. This is a memorable, authentic, and extremely budget-friendly family activity. Watch the Alpine sunset from the resort balcony or a nearby viewpoint — completely free and absolutely spectacular.

meals.breakfast: DIY Swiss breakfast — fresh croissants from a local bakery (CHF 1.50-2 each), Swiss cheese, cold cuts, and coffee/hot chocolate
meals.lunch: Picnic in the snow with supermarket supplies — Swiss bread, cheese, dried meats, fruit, and hot drinks from a thermos. Budget CHF 6-10 per person
meals.dinner: DIY Swiss fondue in the resort — budget CHF 15-20 total for all ingredients from Migros or Coop supermarket

day_by_day.notes: Friday evenings in Swiss ski villages often feature free torchlight ski descents or fireworks displays — check the local event calendar. The supermarket DIY fondue is one of the best budget tips for Switzerland — authentic Gruyère and Emmental cheese are affordable when bought at the supermarket vs. restaurant prices.

day_by_day.morning: Make the most of your ski pass with a full morning on the slopes. Saturday often brings fresh weekend crowds, so hit the lifts early (slopes open around 8:30-9:00 AM) to avoid queues. Try to reach the highest accessible peak on your ski pass for panoramic views of the Swiss Alps — a truly unforgettable experience. Take family photos at designated scenic viewpoints on the mountain.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, switch to family-friendly activities. Build a snowman or have a snowball fight in a designated area near the resort — completely free! Visit the local ski jump or freestyle area to watch professional or advanced skiers perform tricks — usually free to spectate and very exciting for children. Many resorts have free sledding hills separate from the paid toboggan runs — ask at the tourist office.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the penultimate evening of your trip with a slightly more indulgent dinner — try a traditional Swiss mountain restaurant for a set 3-course meal. Look for 'Abendmenü' (evening menu) deals which typically offer better value than à la carte. Share desserts to keep costs down. Reminisce about the week's highlights and plan any last-minute activities for Day 7.

meals.breakfast: Early resort or supermarket breakfast to get on the slopes quickly
meals.lunch: On-mountain self-service cafeteria — choose wisely: soup, bread, and a hot drink (CHF 10-15) rather than full hot meals. Alternatively, bring a packed lunch in a backpack
meals.dinner: Traditional mountain restaurant — 3-course Abendmenü (CHF 28-40 per person). Share a bottle of local Swiss wine (Fendant from Valais is excellent and affordable at CHF 25-35 per bottle)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day at most Swiss ski resorts as weekend visitors arrive. Arrive at lifts 15-20 minutes before opening to secure good position. Consider skiing until the last lift (usually 4:30-5:00 PM) to maximize your ski pass value. Return rental equipment on Sunday morning to avoid extra day charges.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed final morning. Return any rental equipment early to avoid additional charges. Take a final leisurely walk through the Alpine village, visit the local market (Sunday markets in Swiss villages often feature local produce, crafts, and food), and pick up last-minute souvenirs. Swiss chocolate from a supermarket (Lindt, Toblerone, or local brands) makes excellent affordable gifts at CHF 2-8 per bar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout is 11:00-12:00). Store luggage at the resort or train station if needed. Spend the afternoon visiting any remaining sights or activities you may have missed during the week. Take the scenic train or bus back toward Zurich Airport, enjoying the stunning Alpine scenery one last time. The Swiss rail network is punctual and reliable — book return tickets in advance for best prices.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport with plenty of time before departure. Browse the duty-free shops for any final Swiss souvenirs. Enjoy a final Swiss meal at the airport — Coop to go or Migros at the airport offer affordable options. Reflect on an incredible budget-friendly Swiss Alpine adventure filled with skiing, tobogganing, and family memories that will last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or local bakery — treat yourself to a proper Swiss breakfast with fresh Gipfeli (croissants), Bircher muesli, and good Swiss coffee
meals.lunch: Village café or supermarket — keep it light and affordable for travel day (CHF 8-15 per person)
meals.dinner: Zurich Airport — Coop to go or airport restaurant. Budget CHF 15-25 per person. Alternatively, pack leftover supermarket snacks for the flight

day_by_day.notes: Final budget summary tips: Use Swiss Travel Pass for all public transport savings. Always buy supermarket groceries for at least 2 meals per day. Choose group lessons over private ski lessons. Book toboggan runs and activities in advance online for discounts. Total estimated daily budget per person (excluding accommodation and ski passes): CHF 40-70 per day. Have a safe journey home and Auf Wiedersehen from the Swiss Alps!

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Swiss Alps. Check-in, unpack, and settle into your accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival dinner at the resort's in-house restaurant or a light room service meal. Familiarize yourself with the resort amenities, review the week's activity plan, and get a good night's rest to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: Airport/in-flight meal during travel
meals.dinner: Late-night light supper at Aegean Bliss Resort's restaurant or room service — try a warm Swiss soup and bread to ease into local cuisine (approx. CHF 25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is at 22:30, so no sightseeing or activities are planned. Allow at least 60–90 minutes for baggage claim, customs, and transfer to the resort. Pre-arrange a private transfer or taxi from the airport for convenience. Keep Day 2 plans relaxed to allow for jet lag recovery.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort breakfast to recover from travel. After breakfast, take a gentle orientation walk around the resort and nearby village to get acquainted with the surroundings. Visit the local ski rental shop to rent skis, boots, and poles for the family, and pick up lift passes for the Jungfrau Ski Region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Skiing on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes — Begin with beginner-to-intermediate groomed runs to warm up the family. The Jungfrau region offers over 200km of runs, so start with the easier blue runs around Grindelwald or Wengen. Kids and less experienced skiers can take a group ski lesson (approx. CHF 60–80 per person for a 2-hour group lesson).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort, warm up with hot chocolate, and relax tired muscles. Head out for a casual dinner in the nearby village at a traditional Swiss mountain restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or approx. CHF 20–30 per person
meals.lunch: On-mountain ski lodge lunch — try a classic Rösti (Swiss potato dish) or a warm soup at a mid-mountain restaurant (approx. CHF 20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss restaurant in the village — order Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (sliced veal in cream sauce) or a hearty Alpine stew (approx. CHF 35–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ski rentals and lessons in advance to avoid long queues. The Jungfrau region is best accessed from Grindelwald or Lauterbrunnen. Dress in moisture-wicking base layers, insulating mid-layers, and waterproof outer shells. Apply sunscreen — Alpine sun reflects intensely off snow.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride — Depart early from the nearest station (St. Moritz or Zermatt connection point depending on resort location). Board the iconic Glacier Express for a breathtaking journey through the Swiss Alps, crossing 291 bridges and 91 tunnels. Reserve panoramic window seats in advance for the best views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Glacier Express journey through dramatic mountain landscapes, deep gorges, and charming Alpine villages. Enjoy the onboard dining service with a Swiss three-course lunch. Arrive at the destination station and explore the arrival town briefly before returning by regional train.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort or a nearby fondue restaurant to warm up after the scenic train adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — buffet or continental (approx. CHF 20–30 per person)
meals.lunch: Onboard Glacier Express dining car — three-course Swiss meal served at your seat (approx. CHF 45–65 per person, bookable in advance)
meals.dinner: Swiss Cheese Fondue dinner at a cozy local Alpine restaurant — order a classic cheese fondue or raclette for the family (approx. CHF 30–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Glacier Express requires advance reservation, especially for panoramic seats and dining car service. Book tickets at least 2–3 weeks ahead via the Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) website. The full journey runs approximately 8 hours (St. Moritz to Zermatt), but shorter scenic segments can be selected. Swiss Travel Pass holders receive discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Experience — Join a local Alpine cheesemaker for a hands-on morning cooking class in a traditional mountain chalet. Learn the art of making authentic Swiss fondue and raclette from scratch, understand the cheese-making process, and enjoy the fruits of your labor as a mid-morning snack. Great for all ages and a wonderful cultural immersion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes for an afternoon ski session. With a day of skiing already under your belt, try intermediate red runs or explore new areas of the mountain. Families with younger children can enjoy the dedicated kids' ski areas with magic carpet lifts.
day_by_day.evening: Tobogganing on the Fläsch Natural Toboggan Run — Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly winter activities as the sun sets. The natural toboggan run is illuminated on select evenings, creating a magical atmosphere. Rent toboggans at the top and race down the snowy track together.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before the cooking class (approx. CHF 20–30 per person)
meals.lunch: Tasting portions from the fondue-making class serve as a late morning snack; grab a light lunch at a ski lodge café — sandwiches, soup, or a Swiss pretzel (approx. CHF 15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a village pizzeria or international restaurant for a change of pace — pizza, pasta, or a simple Swiss menu (approx. CHF 25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The fondue-making class typically runs 2–3 hours and should be booked in advance through local tour operators or the resort concierge. Toboggan runs may have specific operating hours and evening sessions — confirm times locally. Dress warmly for the toboggan run as temperatures drop significantly after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Family Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking Adventure — Set out on a guided family snowshoeing tour through pristine snow-covered Alpine forests and meadows. Snowshoes and poles are provided by the guide. The trails are suitable for all fitness levels and ages, offering stunning views of the surrounding peaks. Look out for winter wildlife tracks along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoeing adventure or opt for a free afternoon at the resort. Families can enjoy the resort's winter amenities — indoor pool, spa, or a leisurely hot chocolate session on the terrace. Alternatively, explore the nearby village on foot, browse local craft shops for Swiss souvenirs, and visit a local bakery.
day_by_day.evening: Special family dinner experience — visit a traditional Swiss mountain restaurant with live folk music or a cozy fireplace setting. Order a hearty Alpine meal and celebrate the midpoint of the trip with a special dessert like Swiss chocolate fondue.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast to fuel up for the snowshoeing adventure (approx. CHF 20–30 per person)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or trail snacks provided by the snowshoeing guide, or a warm lunch at a mountain hut along the trail — try Alpine cheese bread and hot soup (approx. CHF 15–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Traditional Alpine restaurant with mountain ambiance — order Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), venison stew, or a cheese platter with local wines or non-alcoholic Rivella (approx. CHF 40–60 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the guided snowshoeing tour through the resort concierge or a local outdoor activity company. Tours typically depart in the morning and last 3–4 hours. Wear waterproof boots and warm socks — most guides provide snowshoes and poles. Children as young as 5–6 can participate with appropriate gear.

day_by_day.morning: Final full ski day on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes — Make the most of your last full skiing day. More confident skiers can tackle challenging black runs or off-piste areas with a guide, while families can revisit favorite runs. Consider hiring a private ski instructor for a final improvement session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tobogganing on the Fläsch Natural Toboggan Run (daytime session) — If not experienced on Day 4 evening or for a second thrilling run, enjoy the toboggan run in full daylight for spectacular mountain views. Race down the track multiple times and enjoy the adrenaline rush. Afterward, warm up with a Swiss hot chocolate and Apfelstrudel at a nearby café.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a top-rated local restaurant or the resort's signature dining room. Celebrate the trip with a special Swiss multi-course meal — start with Alpine salad, follow with a main of veal or lake fish, and finish with a Swiss chocolate dessert. Review favorite memories and plan for the journey home.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — make it a full meal to energize for the last ski day (approx. CHF 20–30 per person)
meals.lunch: On-mountain restaurant lunch — treat yourselves to a slightly elevated ski lodge meal, such as a cheese tart, Wiener Schnitzel, or grilled mountain sausages with potato salad (approx. CHF 25–40 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant or a highly-rated local establishment — three-course Swiss dinner with local wine or sparkling water (approx. CHF 55–80 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Return ski and snowboard equipment before the rental shop closes — typically by 18:00. Saturday can be busier on the slopes due to weekend visitors; head to the lifts early (by 08:30) to avoid queues. Begin packing in the evening to prepare for the next day's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — Wake up early for one last look at the stunning Alpine scenery. Take a short leisurely walk around the resort grounds or village to soak in the mountain atmosphere. Visit a local bakery for fresh Swiss bread, croissants, and pastries. Pick up last-minute Swiss souvenirs — chocolates, cheese, or a Swiss army knife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and begin the transfer to the airport. Depending on flight time, stop at a scenic viewpoint en route for a final photo opportunity with the Alps. If time permits, enjoy a quick lunch at a village café or airport restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Arrive at the airport with ample time (minimum 2–3 hours before international flight). Complete check-in, security, and boarding. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, scenic train journeys, cultural experiences, and family adventures in the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a local bakery or resort café — fresh croissants, Swiss bread with butter and jam, and a coffee or hot chocolate (approx. CHF 10–18 per person)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a village café or airport restaurant — sandwiches, soup, or a simple Swiss plate (approx. CHF 20–35 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort (typically 11:00–12:00). Pre-arrange airport transfer the evening before. Allow extra time for mountain road travel, which can be slower in winter conditions. Pack Swiss chocolates and cheese in checked luggage if purchasing perishables. Keep travel documents, passports, and boarding passes easily accessible.

day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival at 22:30. Check in to the Aegean Bliss Resort. A private butler will escort you to your suite. A curated late-night welcome amenity platter (Swiss charcuterie, artisan cheeses, warm Alpine bread, and hot cocoa) will be waiting in-room.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — travel day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — travel day
meals.dinner: In-room late-night welcome platter arranged by the resort: Swiss charcuterie, Gruyère and Emmental cheeses, warm rye bread, house-made fruit preserves, and premium hot chocolate with Alpine cream

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer in advance (Mercedes V-Class or equivalent). Journey from Zurich Airport to the Swiss Alps region is approximately 2–3 hours depending on exact resort location. Confirm with the resort that late check-in is seamlessly arranged. Unpack minimally and rest — a full alpine adventure begins tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort breakfast followed by a guided orientation of the Aegean Bliss Resort's ski concierge. Visit the in-resort ski shop for premium equipment fitting — top-of-the-line Völkl or Salomon skis, custom-fitted boots, and helmets for all family members. Board the resort's private ski shuttle to the Jungfrau Ski Region for your first day on the slopes. A certified private ski instructor will greet the family for a personalized skills assessment and warm-up run on the Kleine Scheidegg area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Skiing on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes — Hit the world-renowned groomed runs of the Jungfrau region. With over 200km of pistes, the private instructor will guide the family through runs suited to each member's skill level. Intermediate and advanced skiers can tackle the iconic Lauberhorn descent, while beginners enjoy the wide, gentle blue runs near Grindelwald First. Take a mid-afternoon break at a mountain hütte for warming refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort via private shuttle. Relax in the resort's alpine spa — heated outdoor pool, sauna, and steam room with panoramic mountain views. Dress for a refined dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grand Alpine Breakfast Buffet at the Aegean Bliss Resort — freshly baked croissants, Swiss bircher muesli, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, seasonal fruit, and barista-crafted coffees
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Grindelwald First or a premium mountain hütte on the Jungfrau slopes — roasted Alpine lamb chops, truffle rösti, warm cheese soup, and mulled wine or hot elderflower for the children
meals.dinner: Signature fine-dining restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — five-course tasting menu featuring pan-seared lake trout, venison medallions with juniper jus, and a Swiss chocolate fondant dessert. Paired with a curated Swiss wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Book private ski instructor at least 48 hours in advance through the resort's ski concierge. Ensure all family members have appropriate ski insurance coverage. Sunscreen is essential even in winter — UV exposure is significantly higher at altitude. The Jungfrau Ski Region is approximately 30–45 minutes from the resort by private shuttle.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on the legendary Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride — one of the world's most breathtaking rail journeys. Depart from Zermatt or St. Moritz (coordinate with resort concierge for optimal boarding point) and glide through dramatic Alpine gorges, frozen rivers, medieval villages, and snow-draped mountain passes. Reserve a First Class panoramic car with floor-to-ceiling windows and a dedicated table for the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Glacier Express journey through the heart of the Swiss Alps, passing over the Landwasser Viaduct and through the Oberalp Pass at 2,033m — the highest point of the route. Enjoy an onboard gourmet lunch service in the panoramic dining car. Disembark at a pre-arranged midpoint station and be collected by a private chauffeur for a scenic drive back to the resort, stopping at a viewpoint for family photos.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a private family movie night arranged by the butler in your suite — popcorn, Swiss chocolates, and warm drinks provided. Alternatively, visit the resort's kids' lounge and game room while parents enjoy cocktails at the Alpine bar.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — buttermilk pancakes with Alpine honey, smoked trout blinis, freshly squeezed juices, and specialty Swiss coffee
meals.lunch: Onboard Glacier Express gourmet dining car — three-course set menu featuring Alpine herb soup, braised Swiss beef with spätzle, and a chocolate and raspberry tart. Swiss mineral water and regional wines included.
meals.dinner: In-suite private dining experience — butler-served fondue for the family: classic Gruyère cheese fondue, beef bourguignon fondue, and a dessert chocolate fondue with seasonal dipping fruits and Swiss brioche

day_by_day.notes: Glacier Express tickets must be booked well in advance — First Class panoramic seats are in high demand during February. Coordinate with the resort concierge to arrange seamless transfers to and from the train stations. The full Zermatt-to-St. Moritz journey takes approximately 8 hours; a partial route can be arranged if preferred for families with younger children. Bring layers — the train is well-heated but station stops can be very cold.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a magical Family Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking Adventure. A certified Alpine guide will meet the family at the resort and lead a private guided snowshoe tour through pristine snow-covered forests and meadows surrounding the resort. Trails are selected based on family fitness levels, with breathtaking views of frozen waterfalls and untouched snowfields. The guide will share fascinating insights about Alpine wildlife, flora, and local mountain traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from the snowshoe tour, head to the Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Experience. Join a local Alpine cheesemaker at a traditional mountain chalet for a hands-on cooking class. The family will learn the art of making authentic raclette and classic Gruyère fondue from scratch — stirring, seasoning, and perfecting the melt. Children will love shaping their own cheese portions and dipping fresh bread into the bubbling pot they created themselves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a well-earned soak in the outdoor thermal pool under the stars. Enjoy a premium après-ski experience at the resort's Alpine lounge — live acoustic Swiss folk music, craft cocktails for adults, and warm spiced apple cider for children. End the evening with a relaxed dinner at the resort's mountain bistro.

meals.breakfast: Early energizing breakfast at the resort — steel-cut oats with Alpine berries, soft-boiled eggs, wholegrain toast with artisan nut butters, and freshly pressed orange juice
meals.lunch: Fondue and raclette feast created during the Swiss Cheese Making Experience — enjoy the fruits of the family's labor with crusty Alpine bread, cornichons, pickled onions, charcuterie, and sparkling Swiss mineral water
meals.dinner: Resort Alpine Bistro — casual yet refined; roasted half chicken with herb jus, truffle mac and cheese (family favorite), warm apple strudel with vanilla bean ice cream, and a selection of Swiss craft beers and premium soft drinks

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe sizes for all family members should be confirmed with the guide in advance. The Swiss Cheese and Fondue Making Experience typically lasts 2–3 hours and is highly interactive for children aged 5 and above. Wear comfortable, warm layers for both activities. The cheesemaking chalet is typically a short drive from the resort — private transfer recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Jungfrau Ski Region for a second day of skiing — this time with a focus on exploring different sectors of the vast ski area. With the private instructor, tackle new terrain: consider the Männlichen plateau for sweeping panoramic views, or the Wengen sector for long, sweeping intermediate runs. For more adventurous family members, arrange a guided off-piste experience in a safe, supervised area with fresh powder exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a mountain lunch, head to the Fläsch Natural Toboggan Run for an exhilarating family tobogganing experience — one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly winter activities. Race down the natural ice-packed run on traditional wooden sleds, with multiple runs available for the whole family. The natural run winds through Alpine forest, offering an authentic and unforgettable Swiss winter experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Treat the family to a premium spa session — children's spa treatments (gentle massages and warm wraps) available alongside adult deep-tissue Alpine herb massages. Conclude the evening with a celebratory dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant to mark the midpoint of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss breakfast at the resort — freshly baked zopf bread, assorted local jams, Appenzeller cheese, cold cuts, soft scrambled eggs, and a Nespresso coffee station
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on the Jungfrau slopes — cheese-topped veal schnitzel, Alpine vegetable soup, hand-cut fries, and warm Rivella (Swiss soft drink) or Glühwein for adults
meals.dinner: Resort fine-dining restaurant — seven-course chef's tasting menu: amuse-bouche, seared foie gras, Alpine mushroom risotto, slow-cooked lamb rack, artisan Swiss cheese board, pre-dessert sorbet, and a Grand Cru chocolate sphere with hazelnut praline. Paired with a Chasselas white wine and Pinot Noir from Graubünden.

day_by_day.notes: Tobogganing at Fläsch or similar natural runs requires advance booking during peak February season. Helmets are mandatory and provided on-site. Confirm the toboggan run's operating hours and accessibility from the resort with the concierge. The transition from skiing to tobogganing in one afternoon is feasible with a private transfer — allow approximately 45 minutes between activities.

day_by_day.morning: A leisurely, relaxed morning at the resort. Sleep in, enjoy a champagne breakfast in bed, and spend time as a family in the resort's dedicated children's activity center — supervised snow sculpting, ice painting, and Swiss crafts workshops keep younger guests entertained while parents enjoy a private yoga or Pilates session with a resort instructor overlooking the Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a private guided cultural excursion to a nearby Alpine village (such as Grindelwald or Mürren) — explore traditional Swiss architecture, browse artisan shops for handcrafted wooden toys, Swiss watches, and local Alpine products. Visit a local confiserie for a Swiss chocolate tasting — sample pralines, truffles, and seasonal specialties crafted by a master chocolatier. End the village tour with a horse-drawn sleigh ride through the snowy village streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a final festive evening. The resort concierge arranges a private igloo dining experience or a fireside outdoor dinner on the resort's heated terrace — wrapped in cashmere blankets under a canopy of Alpine stars. Live music from a classical string quartet or Swiss folk ensemble accompanies the meal.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast in suite — freshly squeezed juices, smoked salmon bagels, Belgian waffles with whipped cream and Alpine berry coulis, and a bottle of chilled Moët & Chandon served by the butler
meals.lunch: Traditional Alpine restaurant in the village — rösti with mountain ham and fried egg, Alpine herb salad, homemade lentil soup, and freshly baked village bread with local butter
meals.dinner: Private outdoor fireside or igloo dining experience at the resort — bespoke menu crafted by the executive chef: lobster bisque, pan-roasted duck breast with cherry reduction, truffle potato gratin, and a flambéed crêpe Suzette for dessert. Champagne and premium Swiss wines throughout.

day_by_day.notes: The horse-drawn sleigh ride should be booked through the resort concierge at least one day in advance — a popular activity during February weekends. The private igloo or outdoor terrace dinner is weather-dependent; the resort will have a backup indoor private dining option. Swiss chocolate tasting can be arranged as a private session with the chocolatier for a more personalized experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast at the resort. Take one last walk through the snow-covered resort grounds — breathe in the crisp Alpine air and capture family photographs with the majestic mountain backdrop. Visit the resort gift shop for premium Swiss souvenirs: artisan chocolates, local liqueurs, handmade scarves, and miniature Swiss chalet keepsakes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer arranged back to Zurich Airport (or Geneva Airport, depending on departure flight). En route, stop at a scenic Alpine viewpoint for a final panoramic farewell to the Swiss Alps. If time permits before the flight, relax in the airport's premium lounge with access arranged through the resort concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. Reflect on an extraordinary week of world-class skiing, scenic train journeys, authentic Swiss cultural experiences, gourmet dining, and cherished family memories in one of the world's most spectacular destinations.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full Swiss and Continental spread: freshly baked croissants and pretzels, Emmental and Gruyère cheese, premium cold cuts, smoked fish, eggs to order, fresh fruit platter, and specialty coffees and teas
meals.lunch: Packed luxury picnic hamper prepared by the resort chef for the journey — artisan sandwiches on sourdough, Swiss cheese wedges, seasonal fruit, Swiss chocolate bars, and sparkling mineral water. Alternatively, dine at a premium airport restaurant if time allows.
meals.dinner: Onboard or at destination — the resort can arrange pre-flight dining coordination or a premium airport restaurant reservation (e.g., Zurich Airport's Yooji's or Swiss Chuchi) if the departure schedule permits

day_by_day.notes: Allow a minimum of 3 hours before your flight for the transfer from the Alpine resort to Zurich Airport, accounting for mountain road conditions in February. Confirm checkout time with the resort and arrange luggage handling through the butler service. Keep a small carry-on with essentials easily accessible. Ensure all ski rental equipment is returned to the resort ski shop the evening before to avoid morning delays. Consider purchasing travel insurance that covers winter sports activities and potential Alpine weather delays.
